purpose: Real result of freezing the Milestone 2 step 3 targeted SEC candidate cohort (2 more prior quarters for the same 23 Milestone 1 issuers), after GitHub Actions' own access to data.sec.gov/submissions/ stayed blocked through 6 consecutive real dispatches (reports/m2-step3-sec-cohort-freeze-blocked-2026-09-30.json).
how_this_differs_from_every_other_real_f: Every prior real SEC freeze (Milestone 1, Milestone 2 step 2) ran nre.depth_cohort.freeze_targeted_candidates() (or nre.cohort.freeze_sec_cohort()) live, from GitHub Actions, via a real PublicClient making the actual HTTPS requests at freeze time. GitHub Actions' own access to data.sec.gov/submissions/ stayed blocked here (6/6 real dispatches, HTTP_403, 2026-09-30 through 2026-10-01). Rather than keep waiting on an external block the project's own history gives no reason to expect will lift (the two other blocked SEC paths from Milestone 3 Phase B have never un-blocked), the owner chose to fetch the same real, public endpoint through the built-in browser instead -- the same transport this project has used before whenever automated access failed (Milestone 1's own SEC freeze, and multiple M3 real-fixture verifications) -- then ran freeze_targeted_candidates() locally with a custom client backed by that real data. The discovery/screening/dedup/validation logic that actually produced the frozen candidates is the exact same, already-tested code every prior freeze used; only the transport (how the bytes got from SEC to this machine) differs.
real_data_integrity: Each of the 23 issuers' real submissions.json was fetched directly from data.sec.gov via the built-in browser, its own real sha256/size recorded (real_source_full_sha256/real_source_full_size in the local, gitignored raw cache), then filtered in-browser to 8-K/8-K-A rows only before being passed to the same real nre.depth_cohort code. The candidate ledger's own discovery_submission_sha256 values describe this filtered, re-serialized form -- labeled explicitly as 'browser_fetched_8k_filtered_subset', never conflated with a hash of SEC's own complete raw response. All 23 fetches were reproduced twice (once for a size check, once for the real run) with byte-identical sha256 hashes both times, confirming the data did not shift between calls.
no_continuation_files_needed: freeze_targeted_candidates() made exactly 23 real client calls (one per issuer) -- confirming none of the 23 issuers needed a continuation file to cover the step-3 window; every real candidate came from each issuer's own 'recent' filings, matching what was predicted when the window was first scoped (every issuer's own real 8-K history reaches comfortably past 2024-11-01).
what_this_is_not: Not yet reviewed for same-day competing catalysts, corporate actions, bell-ambiguous timing, or any of the other by-hand review steps Milestone 1 and Milestone 2 step 2 both required before a candidate becomes an accepted event -- this is discovery only, mirroring exactly what freeze_sec_cohort()/freeze_targeted_candidates() have always produced at this stage.

Not an accepted event set -- config/m2-step3-events.json does not exist yet; building it (and running it through the same-day-catalyst sweep, batching, quarantine/signoff, and real Alpaca dry-runs) is the next phase, the same process Milestone 2 step 2 followed, and needs its own separate owner authorization before starting, per this project's own standing rule against silently moving to the next phase.

Not a claim that GitHub Actions' own access to data.sec.gov/submissions/ is resolved -- it is not; this result was produced entirely without using that blocked path. A future workflow needing live, automated data.sec.gov/submissions/ access from GitHub Actions would hit the exact same HTTP_403 today.
